subject: MedFlux request: temporary 90d debug log retention & CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pri@medflux.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, security@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 90-day debug session retention for MedFlux compliance audit

Hi Jordan + Redwood security team,

Quick one — MedFlux is entering an extended compliance review tied to a recent regulator audit. Our security & compliance group needs evidence that tenant-level session/debug logs for our environment can be retained for 90 days (instead of Redwood's standard 30d) for a 1-month window to support forensic sampling.

Specifically we need:
- Confirmation of which server/session logs are retained by default (names/paths) and whether we can create a tenant-scoped 90d retention for a temporary period (May 15–Jun 15).
- A CAIQ/SIG mapping or SOC2 artifact that shows how retention is handled and proof-of-delete workflow.
- A representative sample (anonymized) of the logs and a short write-up for auditors describing deletion/escrow processes.

Attached is our internal ask doc (MedFlux_LOG_REQUIREMENTS_v1.pdf). Can Redwood provide an evidence bundle and an addendum we can include in our auditor packet? If this requires a formal exception/paperwork we can sign, please flag and send next steps.

Thanks — we need to lock this down quickly.

Priya Shah
CISO, MedFlux
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <pri@medflux.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: 90-day debug session retention for MedFlux compliance audit

Looping you both in — MedFlux wants a temporary tenant-scoped retention bump to 90 days (May 15–Jun 15) and a CAIQ/SIG-aligned evidence bundle. See attached ask from Priya (attached to original).

Proposed immediate asks for internal owners:
1) Neha — can our platform create a per-tenant 90d retention window for debug/session logs without retaining KV cache artifacts? Need cost/SLO impact and whether we can limit to specific log types (session, request traces).
2) Naomi — can you assemble the CAIQ/SIG pointers and a short proof-of-delete narrative and confirm which SOC2 artifact covers this? We may need a signed addendum.

Priya wants a sample anonymized log and a concise write-up for auditors. Can we aim to reply with an approach + expected deliverables by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <pri@medflux.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 90-day debug session retention for MedFlux compliance audit

Jordan / Naomi — quick technical summary and constraints.

What we retain today (default):
- Inference request logs (per-tenant) — includes request id, timestamp, model id, token counts, and hashed tenant identifier. TTL: 30d (configurable).
- System debug traces (service-level) — aggregated and not tenant-linked, TTL: 14d.
- KV cache snapshots (in-memory) — ephemeral, not persisted to disk; not included in retention artifacts.

Feasibility:
- We can provision a tenant-scoped 90d retention for inference request logs for a short window (we have customers on similar exceptions). This requires: a configuration change at the routing/retention layer and a short tear-down runbook after Jun 15.
- We can limit the scope to: inference request logs + per-request routing trace. We should NOT include any in-memory KV cache dumps or PII fields — those are never persisted.

Impact & conditions:
- Cost: roughly +12–18% storage delta for that tenant over the month (rough estimate, billing will show per GB).
- SLO: negligible read/latency impact; longer retention increases restore surface but we will not change serving topology.
- Security controls: data will remain encrypted at rest with tenant key; access will be audit-logged.

Artifacts I can provide: retention-map.csv (lists log types, TTLs, storage locations), forensic-playbook.md (steps for creating window, sampling, and secure deletion). I will redact any internal debug tokens and provide an anonymized log sample.

Action items:
- Naomi: can you map these artifacts to CAIQ idents and confirm SOC2 control references (CC6/CC7 area).
- Jordan: confirm with Priya they accept the limited scope and cost note.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Reliability Engineer — Platform
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: retention-map.csv; forensic-playbook.md)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pri@medflux.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, security@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 90-day debug session retention for MedFlux compliance audit

Priya — thanks for the clear ask and for the doc. Quick summary from our side and next steps: 

What Redwood will provide for the May 15–Jun 15 window:
- A tenant-scoped 90-day retention for inference request logs + per-request routing traces only. We will NOT persist KV cache snapshots or other in-memory-only artifacts.
- An anonymized, auditor-ready log sample and a short write-up describing retention, encryption, and the proof-of-delete workflow.
- A CAIQ/SIG pointer packet and SOC2 control references that show where retention and deletion are covered.
- A formal addendum (medflux_retention_addendum.pdf) that outlines scope, duration, and cost implication (+approx storage delta). This will be DocuSigned once you ACK the scope.

Attachments delivered: redwood_medflux_evidence_bundle.zip (contains anonymized log sample, retention-map.csv, forensic-playbook.md, and CAIQ mapping). medflux_retention_addendum.pdf (terms for the temporary exception).

Related items: JIRA SUP-1234 tracks the provisioning + deletion runbook; DocuSign link in this email will route for signature.

Next steps for MedFlux:
1) Confirm scope acceptance (in writing) — we will not expand retention to additional log types without a separate exception.
2) Sign the addendum (DocuSign) to authorize the change and billing.
3) We will kick provisioning on May 13 (to ensure window starts May 15) and schedule a short validation call May 14.

If this aligns I will hand off to Ops to create the tenant config and Naomi will send the CAIQ mapping.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: redwood_medflux_evidence_bundle.zip; medflux_retention_addendum.pdf)
